name: Decision Trees
description: Decision Trees are non-parametric supervised learning algorithms that create a model in the form of a tree structure. They recursively partition the feature space into regions based on feature values, making decisions through a series of if-else questions until reaching a prediction.

concept.structure: Tree with root node (all data), internal nodes (decision points), branches (outcomes), and leaf nodes (predictions)

splittingCriteria.regression: Mean Squared Error or Mean Absolute Error

concept.explanation: At each node, the algorithm selects the feature and threshold that best separates the data according to the chosen criterion. This recursive process continues until stopping conditions are met.
concept.giniImpurity: 1 - Σ(pᵢ)² where pᵢ is proportion of class i - measures probability of misclassification
concept.informationGain: Parent entropy - weighted average of child entropies

avoidWhen: When overfitting must be strictly avoided

criterion.impact: Gini faster, Entropy more balanced trees

minSamplesSplit.description: Minimum samples required to split internal node

minSamplesLeaf.description: Minimum samples required at leaf node
minSamplesLeaf.impact: Smooths model, prevents leaves with few samples

maxFeatures.description: Number of features to consider for best split

ccpAlpha.description: Complexity parameter for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning

preprocessing: Encode categorical variables (or use algorithm that supports them)
No scaling required (but can help with some implementations)
training: Start with all data at root node
Calculate impurity for each possible split on each feature
Select split with highest information gain / lowest impurity
Recursively split until stopping criteria met
evaluation: Tree depth and number of leaves
interpretation: Follow path from root to leaf for prediction
Feature importance from total reduction in criterion

complexity.timeTraining: O(n × p × log(n)) average, O(n² × p) worst case
complexity.scalability: Moderate - prone to overfitting with depth

cons: Unstable - small data changes alter tree
Greedy algorithm - may not find optimal tree
Biased toward features with more levels

variants.c45: Handles continuous features and missing values
variants.cart: Can handle both classification and regression

regularization: Pre-pruning: Limit depth, min samples per leaf
Post-pruning: Remove branches that don't improve validation
Cost-complexity pruning: Trade-off tree size vs. fit
